chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, linking it up through his chain to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family):
He said: Two men on whom my intercession will not descend: a companion of an oppressive and harsh ruler, and one who is excessive in religion and deviates.
ai.seo_question: Who are the two people excluded from the Prophet's intercession according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies two distinct groups excluded from his intercession: those who serve oppressive, harsh rulers (*sultan 'asuf*) and those who are excessively religious yet deviate from the true path (*gal fi al-din mariq*). This highlights the Shia emphasis on both political justice and theological fidelity, warning against complicity in tyranny and the danger of religious extremism that leads to deviation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-93 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdul Jab’bar who linked it up through a chain of narrators to God’s Prophet (MGB),
“There are two groups on whose behalf I shall not intercede: friends of oppressive kings and those who transgress beyond the religion due to their being excessively religious.”
